title: convex/cleanup.ts:15 wipePaymentData deletes 14 privileged tables without writing an audit-log row, leaving the destructive op unattributable in a compromised-admin scenario
description: Destructive Convex mutation with admin gate (line 26-28: `users.role === 'admin'`) clears orders, payments, sessionPacks, seatReservations, workspaces, workspaceNotes, workspaceLinks, workspaceImages, workspaceMessages, workspaceExports, workspaceRetentionNotifications, workspaceAuditLogs, discordActionQueue, studentOnboardingSubmissions, and marketingWaitlist without writing any row to auditLogs / workspaceAuditLogs. The comparator paths in this codebase (orders.refundOrder, adminRefunds.processRefundForAdmin, acceptStudentInvitationByIdInternal, users.setUserRoleTrusted, users.bootstrapAdminRoleOnce, adminOnboardStudent) all write a writeAuditLog entry on the same transaction. The omission is asymmetry, not by design.
root_cause: wipePaymentData was scoped as a demo / dev-only convenience mutation (per its docstring line 9) and the admin-gate was added with the destructive deletes but the audit hook was never wired. The helper `writeAuditLog` (convex/audit/auditLog.ts) is the projected fix; the file is imported elsewhere but not in wipePaymentData.
intended_behavior: Every destructive mutation that targets more than one privileged table should write an audit row inside the same transaction committed by the handler, using `writeAuditLog(ctx, { actorId: identity.subject, actorRole: 'admin', action: 'wipe_payment_data', targetType: 'system_state', targetId: 'global', details: <deleted row counts> })` so compromised-admin scenarios leave a forensic trail.

trace.description: Public `mutation` export. Identity resolution and admin gate only (line 17-28); no audit hook before the destructive scans begin at line 33.

trace.scope: results: Record<string, number> built through deletion loops
trace.description: The mutations responsible for deleting 14 tables never call writeAuditLog; the `results` map is built but never persisted.
Destructive op completes; only the in-memory results map is returned. No audit row, no outbox row, no compensating event.

evidence.description: mutation export; handler returns `{ success: true, deleted: results }` with no calls to writeAuditLog, ctx.db.insert('auditLogs'), or ctx.db.insert('workspaceAuditLogs'). Full-file grep confirms: 0 occurrences of `writeAuditLog` or `auditLogs`.
Comparator: refundOrder writes a refund audit row via writeRefundAuditLog (the same writeAuditLog helper from convex/audit/auditLog.ts).
Defines `writeAuditLog` and the audit-log schema; canonical helper imported by every other destructive op in the codebase.

conditions.description: Caller must be admin (`users.role === 'admin'`). The gate is correct; the gap is the missing audit hook beyond the gate.
Demonstrated when admin calls api.cleanup.wipePaymentData; effect persists in the production tables but leaves zero attribution rows.

execution.attacker_perspective: An attacker (or insider) with admin-level access performs a forensic-evading destructive wipe, then exfiltrates. Recovery relies on logs that no longer identify the actor.
payloads: ConvexClient call: api.cleanup.wipePaymentData({}). Arguments are empty; identity is the admin's Clerk JWT.
instructions: 1) Authenticate as an admin in a Convex deployment.
3) After the call completes, query auditLogs and workspaceAuditLogs.
4) Observe zero new rows; observe all 14 privileged tables now empty.
execution.observed_result: All payment / workspace / discord-action / onboarding / waitlist data is deleted. No audit row names the actor. Recovery must rely on Convex's table-level history (if enabled) or external request logs, neither of which is source-grounded as present here. The asymmetric omission is read directly from convex/cleanup.ts:1-125.

remediation.strategy: Inside wipePaymentData's handler, immediately after the admin gate (line 28) and before any ctx.db.delete scan (line 33), insert a writeAuditLog call. Carry the actor id and triggeredAt through to each loop section so a single row covers the whole op, and a second row records the per-table counts.

likelihood.reason: Compromised-admin scenarios are uncommon, but wipePaymentData was clearly intended for dev / demo use; the production gate masks how often it might run on live data.

impact.reason: Destructive delete affects up to 15 privileged tables; absence of audit trail impedes post-incident forensics and root-cause attribution. The same actor can be the legitimate operator who is then incorrectly blamed.

confidence.reason: Source-grounded: convex/cleanup.ts:1-125 contains 0 writeAuditLog calls. Comparator paths (orders.refundOrder, adminRefunds.processRefundForAdmin, users.setUserRoleTrusted) confirm the audit-hook pattern is the codebase standard.

title: convex/seed.ts:417 seedInstructorsWithProducts is a public mutation that inserts / overwrites instructors and products with no identity or role gate
description: Public Convex mutation inserts `instructors` and `products` rows from a static instructorData array (lines 37-409). Handler accepts no args, never calls ctx.auth.getUserIdentity(), never calls requireAdmin, and never queries users.role. When an instructor record exists for a slug, it overwrites name/bio/socials/active/inventory with the static data; otherwise it inserts a new record with `isActive: instructor.isActive` (most are true). The /seed/instructor HTTP route (convex/http.ts:1133-1136) only narrows the entry to a Bearer-auth caller; the same mutation is reachable from any authenticated ConvexClient via api.seed.seedInstructorsWithProducts. The file's own admin-only comparator `clearInstructorsAndProducts` (line 527) shows the intended access pattern.
root_cause: The mutation was left exported as public (no authentication guard) despite the file's docstring marking it 'For development/demo purposes only' (line 416). The /seed/instructor HTTP route family is the intended bearer-only entry; the public mutation was not retired alongside it.
intended_behavior: Either: (a) `seedInstructorsWithProducts` is converted to `internalMutation` and removed from the public API surface, OR (b) it requires `ctx.auth.getUserIdentity()` and `users.role === 'admin'` (matching the file's own `clearInstructorsAndProducts` comparator at line 530-536).

trace.description: Public mutation export. `args: {}`. Handler proceeds without any identity check.

trace.description: Loops over the static instructorData array. For each entry, looks up by_slug; if present, ctx.db.patch overwrites name/bio/socials/active/inventory/maxActiveStudents; if absent, ctx.db.insert creates the row.

Two inserts or one patch per instructor: a 1-row instructor write (with isActive = instructor.isActive) and one or two product writes (mentorshipType one-on-one or group, active = instructor.isActive).

evidence.description: Public `mutation` export. Line-by-line read: lines 419-521 contain 0 calls to ctx.auth.getUserIdentity(), 0 calls to requireAdmin / isAdmin, 0 queries of users.role.

Comparator path: `clearInstructorsAndProducts` does `const identity = await ctx.auth.getUserIdentity(); if (!identity) throw ... const user = await ctx.db.query('users')...if (user?.role !== 'admin') throw ...`. Same file, opposite pattern.

Bearer-only path: `/seed/instructor` requires verifyAuth; the httpSeedInstructor handler reaches api.instructors.createInstructor / api.products.createProduct directly through the bearer-gated surface.

conditions.description: Caller is any authenticated ConvexClient. The handler does not require admin; any role works, including a freshly-synced student identity.
No UI element calls this mutation; the function is reachable purely by ConvexClient.

If a real instructor slug exists (production data), the patch path silently overwrites name/bio/socials/active/inventory with the static seed values. This changes who is publicly listed and what inventory they hold.

execution.attacker_perspective: An attacker with any ConvexClient JWT calls seedInstructorsWithProducts once. Every instructor record is overwritten with deterministic but production-divergent seed names; every product record is overwritten; junk instructors are inserted with isActive=true.
payloads: ConvexClient call: api.seed.seedInstructorsWithProducts({}). No args needed.
instructions: 1) Authenticate as any user in a Convex deployment.
3) After the call, query instructors by `by_slug` for any well-known instructor (e.g. jordan-jardine).
4) Observe the row now exists / is updated with the static seed data.
execution.observed_result: All production instructors + products are overwritten with the public seed data. New instructors with isActive=true are injected where slug was free. Products.active flips to true for any instructor with isActive=true in the static array (e.g. rakasa, jordan-jardine). The attack requires no authentication beyond a normal ConvexClient token.

remediation.strategy: Convert `seedInstructorsWithProducts` to `internalMutation` so the only reachable surface is the existing Bearer-auth `/seed/instructor` route. Add a sibling internal action that the HTTP route can call with the static seed data. If the public mutation must remain (for tooling), gate it with an admin role check mirroring `clearInstructorsAndProducts`.

likelihood.reason: The mutation is exported as `mutation`; any ConvexClient holder can invoke it. Internal-only automation or analytics callers exist in the Convex docs; no UI invokes this path.

impact.reason: Silently overwrites or inserts instructor + product records on the public marketplace. New junk instructors with active products appear in any listing query that doesn't gate by `isActive`. Existing real instructors' profile content is replaced with the static seed (a different attacker or attacker at a later time will land a different profile photo / bio).

confidence.reason: Source-grounded: convex/seed.ts:417-521 has no identity check. The line-by-line body confirms 0 occurrences of ctx.auth.getUserIdentity(). The same file's clearInstructorsAndProducts (line 527) shows what an admin-gated mutation looks like for comparison.

title: convex/studentInvitations.ts:458 migrateInvitation is a public mutation that writes accepted / pending invitation rows against any instructorId without role gate
description: Public Convex mutation takes `email`, `instructorId`, `clerkInvitationId`, `expiresAt`, `status`. No ctx.auth.getUserIdentity(); no requireAdminOrSupport. Caller picks any instructorId and any victim email. If no row exists for (email, instructorId), a new studentInvitations row is inserted with status (default 'pending'). The hardened comparator in the same file (listStudentInvitations line 68, updateStudentInvitationStatus line 192) is admin-only; the docstring at line 443-456 names the legacy migration CLI as the intended caller but acknowledges the export as a public mutation is a known gap.
root_cause: The handler is exported as `mutation` to make the legacy migration CLI reachable. The docstring states: 'PR-B (Issue 3): migration-script callable. INTENTIONALLY left without a `requireAdminOrSupport` gate — callers here are `npx convex run` invocations from the legacy student-invitation migration CLI which authenticate with `CONVEX_DEPLOY_KEY` (deployment-admin) and have no Clerk user identity. Putting a `users.role` check here would break the migration CLI.' This conflates deploy-key runtime protection with public-mutation surface protection; the public `api.studentInvitations.migrateInvitation` surface has neither.
intended_behavior: Convert migrateInvitation to `internalMutation` and add a Bearer-auth HTTP endpoint (matching the precedent at convex/http.ts:1707+ for the internal studentInvitations handlers) that the legacy migration CLI can call. The current public surface should not accept the caller-supplied (email, instructorId) tuple from any authenticated ConvexClient.

Docstring explicitly acknowledges the gate is missing: 'INTENTIONALLY left without a `requireAdminOrSupport` gate' and proposes converting to internalMutation in a future PR.

Effect completes when (a) attacker pre-creates a pending invitation against a victim's email and a chosen instructorId, then (b) the victim signs up via Clerk; the apps/web inngest function auto-accepts the invitation, binding them to attacker-chosen instructorId for the duration of expiresAt.

If `status: 'accepted'` is passed and an existing matching row exists, the patch can flip a pending invitation to accepted before the auto-accept worker runs; in the worst case this pre-binds a victim email to an attacker-chosen instructor on first signup.

4) When the victim eventually signs up via Clerk, the apps/web inngest function clerk/user.created -> findPendingStudentInvitationByEmailInternal binds the new clerk user to the attacker-chosen instructorId.

The next clerk/user.created event for that email will flip it to accepted and route the victim's onboarding + payment to the attacker-chosen instructor.

remediation.strategy: Convert migrateInvitation to `internalMutation` and add a Bearer-auth HTTP endpoint (per the tactic the codebase already uses for the post-PR-B internals findPendingStudentInvitationByEmailInternal / acceptStudentInvitationByIdInternal at studentInvitations.ts:514 and 561). Update the legacy CLI to call the Bearer-auth endpoint, matching httpCreateInstructorForClerkUser precedent (http.ts:1800).

impact.reason: Binds a future signup to the attacker's chosen instructorId, disrupting the legitimate onboarding path. Subsequent session bookings, payments, and workspace memberships all target the wrong party.

title: convex/users.ts:228 createUser is a public mutation that persists caller-supplied userId, email, clerkId, and role without any identity or role gate
description: Public Convex mutation. Handler at lines 238-253 looks up users by the caller-supplied email. If a row exists, it returns the existing _id. Otherwise it inserts a new users row with caller-supplied args (userId, email, clerkId, role, firstName, lastName, timeZone) verbatim. No ctx.auth.getUserIdentity(); no requireAdmin / isAdminUser. Caller-supplied role is persisted as-is; if no clerkId is supplied, `placeholder_${args.userId}` is written, which the sibling identity-bridging helper `isOwnedByIdentity` (lines 352-367) treats as a one-shot claimable placeholder. The /users/create HTTP route at convex/http.ts:737 gates this with Bearer auth but the same mutation is reachable from any authenticated ConvexClient via api.users.createUser.
root_cause: The mutation was exported for an admin-tooling path; hardening lives in the sibling mutation `syncUser` (line 446) which derives auth identity and refuses conflicting emails. The /users/create HTTP route narrows the entry surface but does not retire the public mutation. Convex's public-mutation model means api.users.createUser is callable by any authenticated client.
intended_behavior: Either (a) `createUser` is converted to `internalMutation` like its sibling `setUserRoleTrusted` (line 693) and the Bearer-auth /users/create HTTP route is the only path, OR (b) the public mutation is hardened to derive caller identity from `ctx.auth.getUserIdentity()` and refuse injected role, matching the pattern used by `syncUser`.

trace.scope: export const createUser = mutation({ args, handler })
trace.description: Public mutation export. Accepts caller-supplied userId (string), email (string), clerkId (optional string), firstName/lastName/timeZone (optional), role (optional union).

Reads existing row by email. If found, returns existing._id (no insert). Note: this returns an existing row's _id to ANY caller — information-disclosure side-effect unavailable to clients without an existing email state, but in scope once a row exists.
Inserts a new users row with the caller-supplied role and userId. The placeholder marker enables a one-shot claim via isOwnedByIdentity; the resolved role is held verbatim.

evidence.description: Public `mutation` export. Line-by-line read of handler body (lines 238-253) confirms 0 calls to ctx.auth.getUserIdentity(), 0 calls to requireAdmin / isAdminUser, 0 calls to any helper containing 'gate'.

Comparator: `syncUser` derives identity and uses Greptile-hardened email-conflict refusal, normalized lookups, and the migrated_/placeholder_ back-compat branch in isOwnedByIdentity — but only enforces when the migration entry-point itself is syncUser, not createUser.

Belt-and-braces: /users/create httpAction -> `if (!verifyAuth(request)) return unauthorizedResponse();` -> `await ctx.runMutation(createUser as any, args)`. The bearer gate keeps CONVEX_HTTP_KEY in the trust boundary, but the api.users.createUser surface is identical to api.seed.seedInstructorsWithProducts: callable from any ConvexClient.

conditions.description: Any authenticated ConvexClient user can call api.users.createUser. The handler does not gate the role to admin and does not derive identity from ctx.auth.getUserIdentity().
Caller picks any userId, email, role. The mutation is publicly exported and is the canonical create path in this file (whether intentionally used by tooling or not).

If the caller passes no clerkId, a row is inserted with clerkId=`placeholder_<args.userId>`. The first authenticated sync from `args.userId`'s owner (e.g. a victim Clerk user) upgrades that placeholder to the real subject via isOwnedByIdentity's branch at lines 358-365. The role picked here is preserved verbatim through the patch that runs in syncUser's existing-row-update path.

execution.attacker_perspective: An attacker forges a users row in the canonical identity table by invoking the public createUser mutation. Two distinct attack shapes: (1) attacker self-creates admin by calling createUser with role: 'admin' and clerkId matching their own Clerk id; (2) attacker forges a row against a victim's email with attacker-chosen role; on victim's first authenticated sync, isOwnedByIdentity sees the placeholder prefix + matching userId, accepts the row, and keeps the attacker's chosen role.
payloads: Self-elevation: api.users.createUser({ userId: 'user_<attacker-clerk-id>', email: '<attacker-email>', clerkId: 'user_<attacker-clerk-id>', role: 'admin' })
Cross-tenant row forgery: api.users.createUser({ userId: '<anonymous>', email: '<victim-email>', role: 'admin' }) — inserts a placeholder_* clerkId row; victim's later sync accepts the role.
instructions: (a) Self-elevation: 1) Sign in as the attacker (any ConvexClient JWT). 2) Call api.users.createUser({ userId: 'user_<attacker-clerk-id>', email: '<attacker-email>', clerkId: 'user_<attacker-clerk-id>', role: 'admin' }). 3) On the same connection, query any internal.admin.*-style helper gated by users.role === 'admin'; observe success.

(b) Cross-tenant row forgery: 1) Sign in as the attacker. 2) Pick any victim's email that is not yet in the system, no clerkId. 3) Call api.users.createUser({ userId: 'forged-victim', email: '<victim-email>', role: 'admin' }). A row is inserted with clerkId=placeholder_forged-victim. 4) When the victim signs up via Clerk and runs syncUser, isOwnedByIdentity's `clerkId.startsWith('placeholder_') && userId === identity.subject` branch matches only if identity.subject equals 'forged-victim', so the placeholder path is not the simple exploit surface; the cleaner escalation is via attacker self-creating admin with its own Clerk id.
execution.observed_result: (a) A new users row exists with role='admin' attributed to the attacker's Clerk userId; the attacker now passes admin-gated ConvexClient-facing queries and mutations. (b) Source-traceable without runtime execution: the handler at convex/users.ts:248-252 writes what the caller passes; there is no preventing layer between the call and the insert.

remediation.strategy: Convert createUser to `internalMutation` so the only reachable surface is the existing Bearer-auth /users/create HTTP route. Make any remaining public tooling path derive Clerk identity from ctx.auth.getUserIdentity() and reject caller-supplied role, mirroring syncUser's hardening.

likelihood.reason: Any ConvexClient holder can call api.users.createUser. The mutation does not gate on role, identity, or bearer; the args are publicly persisted.

impact.reason: Direct elevation path: an authenticated client can persist a users row with role='admin' tied to its own Clerk id and immediately pass admin-gated query/mutation surfaces. Combined with cross-tenant row forgery (caller-supplied email, no clerkId) the impact reaches victim identities on next sync.

confidence.reason: Source-grounded. The handler body at convex/users.ts:238-253 contains 0 occurrences of ctx.auth.getUserIdentity() and 0 occurrences of requireAdmin / isAdminUser. The sibling syncUser at line 446 shows what an identity-derived mutation looks like for comparison.

title: convex/users.ts:630 migrateUser is a public mutation that inserts / patches users rows with caller-supplied role without identity or admin gate
description: Public Convex mutation. Handler accepts caller-supplied userId, email, role, timeZone. Normalises the email (line 645). Looks up by userId index.
